Shriram General Insurance Company ... vs Thalary Hemalatha
on 9 July, 2025
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty

Judgment:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present appeal is filed by the appellant-insurance Company, aggrieved by the Order dated 17.10.2023 in M.V.O.P.No.25 of 2019, passed by the learned Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Medak.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Medak
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The appellant herein is the respondent No.3, respondents No.1 to 4 are claimants and respondents No.5 and 6 are respondents No.1 and 2, before the Tribunal.

3. Heard Sri Harinath Reddy Soma, learned Counsel for the appellant and Sri A.Yadava Reddy,
learned Counsel for respondents No.1 to 4.
4.

The brief facts of the case, which led to filing of the present appeal, are that respondents No.1 to 4 filed claim petition vide M.V.O.P.No.25 of 2019, seeking compensation on account of death of one Thalary Yellaiah (deceased), in a road accident that took place on 02.03.2019.

The deceased was travelling on a motor cycle bearing No.TS 15 EV 3890, as a pillion rider, which was driven by the respondent No.6.
5.
Before the Tribunal, on behalf of claimants, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.P1 to P6, were marked.
On behalf of the respondents, R.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Ex.R1 was marked.

6. The Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, awarded Rs.12,00,000/- as compensation along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization and fastened liability on appellant and respondents No.5 and 6 jointly and severally.

The Tribunal further directed the appellant herein to first pay the compensation and gave liberty to the appellant to recover the same from respondent No.5 (owner) and respondent No.6 (driver).
7.

The learned Counsel for the appellant would submit that the driver of the motor cycle did not possess a valid Driving License as on the date of accident and he was charge sheeted under Section 304-A IPC and Section 181 and 196 of Motor Vehicles Act, therefore appellant is not liable to pay compensation.
He also submitted that it is the statutory duty of the owner of the vehicle to see that the driver to whom the vehicle is entrusted holds an effective driving license to drive such vehicle.
Since there is clear violation of the conditions of the policy, appellant cannot be made liable to pay compensation.

He further submitted that claim petition is filed under Section 163-A of M.V.Act, and therefore the annual notional income of the deceased should not cross Rs.40,000/- and future prospects also cannot be granted.
However, the Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased as Rs.8,000/- per month and also considered the future prospects @ 10% and awarded a sum of Rs.12,00,000/-, contrary to schedule-II.
Therefore, prayed to allow the present appeal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Counsel for respondents No.1 to 4 would submit that though the application was filed under Section 163-A of M.V.Act, entire evidence was adduced as per Section 166 of M.V.Act.

Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly considered the application under Section 166 of M.V.Act and awarded just and reasonable compensation, and no grounds are made out to interfere with the award passed by the Tribunal.

He further submitted that respondents No.1 to 4 have filed an application vide I.A.No.4 of 2024, to amend the provision of law of the claim petition from Section 163-A to 166 of M.V.Act, and this Court vide Order dated 01.04.2025, allowed the said application, and therefore, the contention of the appellant that the Tribunal has awarded the amount contrary to Schedule-II of the M.V.Act when the claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of M.V.Act,
is not tenable.
9. Perusal of the record would disclose that respondents No.1 to 4-claimants are claiming that deceased was a contractor labour and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

In the absence of any evidence on record to substantiate the said claim, the Tribunal considered the deceased as unskilled labour earning daily wages and fixed the monthly income as Rs.8,000/-, as per the Minimum Wages Act and deducted 1/3rd of the income towards personal expenses.

The Tribunal has considered the age of the deceased as 30 years basing on Ex.P3-inquest report and applied multiplier 17 and has also awarded future prospects at 10% and awarded Rs.12,00,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum.

10. The Tribunal basing on the pleadings placed on record, as well as the charge sheet filed against respondent No.6 for the offence under Section 304-A IPC, has come to the conclusion that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.6, and that there is no fault on the part of the driver of the R.T.C bus.
The Tribunal has also observed that the charge sheet was filed under Section 181 of M.V.Act, as the respondent No.6 did not produce valid Driving License.

The Tribunal finally concluded that since there is valid insurance policy, appellant herein is liable to pay the compensation amount and thereafter, recover the same from respondents No.5 and 6, by applying the principle of Pay and Recovery, by relying upon the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others 1.
11.

entities.text: Shamanna and another Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Limited and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of the above discussion, this Court does not find any reason or ground to interfere with the Award passed by the tribunal and further the tribunal has rightly ordered the appellant to first pay the compensation to the claimant and then recover the same from respondents No.5 and 6,
as the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.6, and thus the appeal is devoid of merits, and accordingly dismissed.
No costs.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
